claims.claim: H1: on 418 held-out T1 tasks (75 commits), graphify's code layer has 0.564 recall inside 8,000 tokens against 0.700 for the typed graph. Difference -0.137 [-0.188, -0.088]; typed is 'better' by the declared rule.
claims.detail: The rule is applied exactly. The signs are negative on T1, T2 and T3, but the T3 sign rests on -0.018 [-0.175, +0.135]. Dropping five commits favourable to typed gives -0.100 [-0.141, -0.060]; dropping five favourable to graphify gives -0.161 [-0.212, -0.114]. Seeds matched by id only: -0.118 [-0.165, -0.072]. Adapter mapping loss is zero: every returned file exists in the shared facts. The qualification to add: graphify's order puts large files first (422 against 247 tokens per shown file). On measures that do not charge for file size the gap is smaller: top-10 file recall -0.102 [-0.145, -0.060], nDCG@10 -0.063 [-0.095, -0.032], MRR -0.015 [-0.055, +0.027], which includes zero. Exact wording: 'On recall of the changed files and definitions inside an 8,000-token answer, on this repository, the typed graph scored higher than graphify's code layer queried through our adapter. Part of the gap is graphify ranking large, highly connected files first under a size-charged budget. The first right file comes equally early in both.'

claims.claim: H2: against scripted search, the changed-together floor and the same-folder floor the verdict is 'inconclusive' each time.
claims.detail: The verdicts follow the rule. G-2 and G-3 miss 'better' only because T3 has the opposite sign (25 tasks, 4 parents). The sensitivity check was reported in one direction only. Dropping graphify's five best commits gives G-2 -0.099 [-0.166, -0.037] and G-3 -0.115 [-0.184, -0.051], both excluding zero. Dropping the floor's five best gives G-4 +0.067 [+0.013, +0.121] with T2 and T3 positive, which would read 'better' for graphify. Seeds matched by id only, the addendum 6 item 12 check that was not reported: no verdict changes. On secondary ranking measures graphify is above the same-folder floor: nDCG@10 +0.093 / +0.164 / +0.286 on T1 / T2 / T3, all excluding zero. Exact qualification: 'inconclusive means neither better nor equivalent is supported. Each of these verdicts moves with five of 75 commits.'

claims.claim: H3: where the seed lives decides most of this. Mobile: -0.019 vs typed, +0.131 [+0.038, +0.215] vs scripted search. Backend: -0.227 vs typed, -0.214 vs search.
claims.detail: The numbers reproduce, but 'decides' is causal wording. The backend gap is robust at 8,000 tokens (3 commits higher for graphify, 37 lower vs typed). Graphify's top files on backend are level with scripted search: top-10 recall -0.035 [-0.103, +0.024], nDCG@10 -0.001, MRR +0.071 [-0.003, +0.135]. The backend gap grows with budget. The mobile lead over search is fragile: dropping five commits gives +0.066 [-0.024, +0.141]; at 2,000 tokens +0.001; at 4,000 +0.048; top-10 recall, nDCG and MRR are all slightly negative with intervals including zero. Graphify being close to typed on mobile holds only at 8,000 tokens (2,000 tokens: -0.080 [-0.148, -0.020]). The typed graph shows the same mobile pattern, because history-based arms are weak there. The held-out mix (36 % mobile seeds against 17 % on tuning) favours graphify. Exact wording: 'graphify's shortfall is concentrated on backend seeds and grows with answer size. On mobile seeds it scored above scripted search and both floors at 8,000 tokens, but not at 2,000 or 4,000, not on top-10 ranking, and not after dropping five commits.'

claims.claim: H4: of 336 T1 reference files reachable only through route, table, setting or changed-together links, graphify showed 0 (typed 66, search 91). On the other 2,226 files: 0.604 / 0.722 / 0.613.
claims.detail: The 0 holds by construction: graphify builds none of those link kinds. Within 3 hops the same split gives 14 of 210. The group split does not isolate link kinds as a cause. With an unbounded walk the NEEDS group equals the cross-runtime set (82 tasks, 9 commits). In the WITHOUT group the typed arm still ranks with co-change edges. Tuning-only indication: typed restricted to parser-type classes at 2 hops scored 0.608, its all-class 2-hop base 0.664, its frozen primary 0.785, and graphify's chosen configuration 0.682. Link kinds and tuned traversal together carry the typed lead, and the run cannot separate them. Exact wording: '13 % of T1 reference files (336 of 2,562, on 82 of 418 tasks) are out of graphify's reach by construction. Tasks without them still show -0.134, and this run does not split that between link kinds, ranking and tuning.'

claims.claim: H5: graphify's native default answer text (median 2,182 tokens) named 0.344 of T1 reference files, against 0.447 typed and 0.360 scripted search at 2,000 tokens.
claims.detail: Recomputed at 0.3443. The headline needs its intervals: vs typed -0.102 [-0.172, -0.033]; vs search -0.015 [-0.097, +0.068]; vs both floors the intervals include zero. The native form tells the same story as the packed form. Adapter effect: the query text '<name> <path>' lets path words start the search elsewhere (median 11 % of printed nodes in another part of the app). Without the 39 answers that mostly drift, recall is 0.351, so the effect is negligible. Limits to attach: this is keyword mode at depth 2, not the frozen seeded mode, and file paths only are credited.

claims.claim: H6: on 30 held-out questions graphify's answer to the question text scored macro F1 0.072 (typed 0.745, search 0.645), with median 2,547 answer tokens against 31 and 29.5.
claims.detail: F1 is driven by precision, because the answer is a traversal printout naming about 26 candidates. Recall is the fair reading: 0.194 at the default budget and 0.347 at budget 8000, against 0.808 and 0.789. The headline breaks addendum 6 item 14: scripted search read a median 694.5 tokens, and the typed per-kind query programs are not counted. The adapter passed the question verbatim, with its '[repo at commit ...]' prefix, to a lexical matcher, and skipped graphify's documented agent step that picks vocabulary words. 24 of 30 questions need links graphify does not build. Exact wording: 'Given the raw question text, with no agent and no vocabulary step, graphify's code-layer printout contained 0.19 of the reference items (0.35 at 8,000 tokens), against 0.81 and 0.79 for per-kind answers whose own costs are counted differently.'

claims.claim: Limits: tuning effort (10 against 60 configurations), build cost, and code layer only.
claims.detail: The three full-traversal configurations converge at 0.671 to 0.688 on tuning, so more shipped options are unlikely to close a 0.10 gap. Non-default relation lists, context filters and padding were not tried. On tuning graphify was below every comparator, including the same-folder floor (0.682 against 0.719); RESULT.md does not say this. Graphify's purpose-built 'affected' command scored 0.20 on tuning: it walks only toward dependents. Build times are not comparable, because the typed facts' conditions were not recorded.

claims.claim: Owner question: why graphify shows good results while this test found little.
claims.detail: Supported: on the first test's own tasks, graphify's code layer did not find more changed files than arms the first test already had. It showed no capability that test lacked. This is consistent with graphify's published numbers measuring other things: answer size against the whole corpus with no correctness check, conversational memory, 6 agent questions on another repository. Not supported: anything about tokens (every answer filled its budget and no session ran), the model-read document layer, an agent using graphify, other repositories, or orientation tasks. The task fit is partial. 'query' is an orientation tool for an agent that reads and asks again. 'affected' covers one direction of a change. Neither was designed to rank the files to edit.
